title: HATSolver: Learning Gröbner Bases with Hierarchical Attention Transformers
claim: Structured sequential data can be represented as a tree, from whole system down to individual tokens, enabling hierarchical modeling.
layout: single tree diagram, top-down, branching three levels to token leaves
description: A single monospace-font tree drawn with thin black lines on a white background. The root, 'System', sits at the top and splits into two children, 'Equation 1' and 'Equation 2'. Each equation splits into two term nodes, labeled 'Term 1' and 'Term 2'. Each term branches into four leaf tokens along the bottom row. The leaves read '<bos> C1 E2 E2', '+ C5 E2 E1', '<SEP> C3 E3 E0' and '+ C2 E1 E0'. They show each term as a coefficient token followed by exponent tokens, with special tokens for start, separator and plus. There is no color, no icons and no arrows. The eye goes first to the root, then follows the symmetric branching down to the token sequence.
caption: Hierarchical representation of the tokenized system of equations p1 = x2
abstract: At NeurIPS 2024, Kera et al. introduced the use of transformers for computing Groebner bases, a central object in computer algebra with numerous practical applications. In this paper, we improve this approach by applying Hierarchical Attention Transformers (HATs) to solve systems of multivariate polynomial equations via Groebner bases computation. The HAT architecture incorporates a tree-structured inductive bias that enables the modeling of hierarchical relationships present in the data and thus achieves significant computational savings compared to conventional flat attention models. We generalize to arbitrary depths and include a detailed computational cost analysis. Combined with curriculum learning, our method solves instances that are much larger than those in Kera et al. (2024 Learning to compute Groebner bases)
